series: Things Living In Your House, Part 20
sources: University of Kentucky Entomology, ENTFACT-439 Sowbugs & Pillbugs: isopods, crustaceans that live on land; seven pairs of legs; pillbugs roll into a ball, which also retains water, sowbugs cannot and have two tail-like uropods; eat decaying plant matter and fungi, sometimes seedlings; do not bite or sting, harmless; females carry eggs and young in a brood pouch (marsupium); live about 3 years; come indoors for moisture and struggle without high humidity; https://entomology.mgcafe.uky.edu/ef439
UF/IFAS EDIS IG093, Pillbugs and sowbugs: the only crustaceans fully adapted to land; beneficial nutrient recyclers; https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IG093

title: Touch This Bug in Your Basement and It Rolls Into a Ball
tiktok_caption: pillbugs (roly polys) in my basement 🐚 they aren't insects, they're crustaceans like crabs and shrimp, and they roll into a ball to hold in water. Would you let one crawl on your hand? ✋ yes / 🙅 no #pillbug #rolypoly #bugsinyourhouse #meatballmyths #learnontiktok

beats.say: Touch the armored bug in your basement. It rolls into a ball.
It's not an insect. It's a cousin of crabs.
Seven pairs of legs, seven armor plates.
It eats dead leaves and fungus.
The only crustaceans that fully moved onto land.
Subscribe. Next: termites eating your house from the inside.
